finalYearProjects.title: Efficient Video Reconstruction Using VAE for Compressive Sensing
finalYearProjects.subtitle: B.Tech final-year project
finalYearProjects.tags: Python · Compressive sensing · Neural networks · Autoencoders
finalYearProjects.description: A B.Tech final-year project that reconstructs video from far fewer samples than conventional capture requires. Instead of storing every full-resolution frame, the system acquires only a small set of linear measurements and recovers the original frames from them. A Python pipeline extracts frames, applies the measurement process and trains a variational autoencoder (VAE) that learns a compact latent representation of the video. That learned prior then guides reconstruction, so the model can rebuild frames from highly incomplete data rather than relying on classical solvers alone. The work studies the trade-off between compression ratio, reconstruction quality and compute cost.
highlights: Compressive sensing: recover video from a small set of linear measurements instead of full-resolution capture.
VAE prior: a variational autoencoder learns a compact latent space that guides and regularises reconstruction.
Python pipeline: frame extraction, measurement sampling, model training and frame-level reconstruction.
Trade-off study: compression ratio versus reconstruction quality versus compute cost.
finalYearProjects.realWorldValue: More bandwidth-efficient streaming and video processing, with cheaper capture and storage on resource-constrained devices.

finalYearProjects.title: Centralized Streetlight Fault Detection & Location Tracking
finalYearProjects.subtitle: B.Tech final-year project
finalYearProjects.description: A B.Tech final-year project that turns ordinary streetlights into a monitored smart-city network. Each pole carries an ESP32 node with LDR/IR sensing that detects whether the lamp is actually lit, dims brightness when no vehicle is present and flags faults such as a blown lamp or a dark pole. Fault events are sent over GSM to a central dashboard together with the pole's identity and location, so maintenance crews are dispatched to the exact lamp instead of patrolling an entire street. The nodes are built for low cost and low power: they run unattended, report only on state changes and can be deployed pole by pole as the network grows.
highlights: ESP32 nodes with LDR/IR sensing to detect lamp status and vehicle presence.
Adaptive dimming that lowers brightness when the road is empty to save energy.
GSM fault alerts carrying pole ID and location straight to a central dashboard.
One centralized view of every pole for faster, targeted maintenance.
finalYearProjects.realWorldValue: Energy savings, safer lit streets and faster smart-city maintenance.

education.description: B.Tech in Electronics and Communication Engineering at Presidency University, Bengaluru — the engineering base behind everything I build. Coursework covered core electronics, signal processing, communication systems and embedded logic, with programming in Python and C/C++ and plenty of lab work that turned theory into working circuits and code. The degree closed with two applied builds: an efficient video reconstruction system using a VAE for compressive sensing, and a centralized streetlight fault detection and location tracking network built on ESP32.
highlights: Core ECE: electronics, signal processing, communication systems and embedded logic.
Programming and problem solving: Python, C/C++, data handling and system design fundamentals.
Hands-on labs: circuits, sensors, embedded boards and prototypes built from scratch.
Final-year builds: VAE video reconstruction and an ESP32 streetlight monitoring network.

education.description: Joined the Indian Startup School accelerator to learn how a venture is actually built, not just how it is described in a classroom. The program covered venture building, product-market fit, business execution and growth strategy, and pushed me to develop my own startup idea through validation, positioning and go-to-market thinking. Just as valuable was the network — founders, mentors and peers I can reach out to for feedback, partnerships and practical advice when I take my own product to market.
highlights: Why I joined: to learn how to build my own startup instead of only studying business theory.
Venture building: idea validation, product-market fit, execution and growth strategy.
Founder mindset: pitching, positioning and taking a product from concept to market.
Network: founders, mentors and peers for feedback, partnerships and go-to-market advice.
